Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

daos (development version)

  • Validation checkpoints are extended into a small family that shares one engine (vignette("validation")):

    • expect_none() checks a condition and returns the full data, so checks can be chained mid-pipeline.
    • expect_unique() checks keys, e.g. before a join.
    • expect_balanced() checks that a register panel is balanced, or with gaps_only = TRUE that units do not skip periods.
    • expect_no_overlap() checks that spells (addresses, employment) do not overlap within a unit.
    • tally_violations() counts violations for many rules at once without warning or aborting; filter and pipe it into expect_empty() to judge.

  • expect_empty() failure messages now give the row count and preview the first rows. Messages are shown literally (braces are no longer interpolated). With warn_msg or abort_msg set, the success message defaults to "Check passed: <message>", so the log names every check. Failures signal class daos_check_failure with the rows in $violations. Log lines now include the row count. New dump argument writes offending rows to CSV; log and dump default to the options daos.check_log and daos.check_dump.

  • age(year) defaults to primo = "previous_ultimo": opening ages on 31 December of the previous year. Use primo = "jan1" for 1 January ages.

  • write_excel() gains digits: keep zero displayed decimals by default, choose a different precision, or use NULL to disable automatic numeric formatting. Stored values are unchanged.

  • Consolidate Excel writing in write_excel(mode = ...): new (default), append, replace (matching sheets), and overwrite (entire workbook). Remove append_excel() and the former overwrite argument.

  • Excel exports now write numeric missing values as blank cells and handle all-missing numeric columns without warnings. Invalid or duplicate sheet names and invalid list inputs are rejected before writing. mode = "replace" matches sheet names ignoring case and preserves replaced sheets’ positions.

  • Add inspect_db() to diagnose mixed full DB07/DB25 codes, returning key membership and both labels. Shared codes remain unresolved, even if labels match; unknown and missing codes receive explicit statuses.

  • Add db_label() to look up Danish industry titles from bundled DST tables for DB25 or DB07, including hierarchy codes. Requires an explicit version. Accepts dotted or compact input; unknown codes warn and return NA.

  • Add convert_db07_to_db25() and convert_db25_to_db07() using bundled DST keys (source page updated 26 February 2026). Both accept mixed code formatting and offer dotted or compact output. The default strict method warns and returns NA for splits; method = "simple" uses DST’s separate approximate matrix for each direction. Invalid or unknown full codes also warn and return NA.

  • add_cpr_info() now accepts selections such as sex, bday, and alder = age(year, "ultimo"). Multiple age references work in one call. This replaces the add, ref_date, year, and at arguments.

  • age(year) uses the previous 31 December; age(date = ...) accepts an explicit date. Bare age uses today. Default output still includes all five information types.

  • add_cpr_info() preserves the source CPR column. Use clean_cpr() explicitly to standardise it. Existing output columns require overwrite = TRUE; duplicate output names and replacing the source CPR column are errors.

  • CPR cleaning and derivation now share a registered native C kernel. Each CPR is parsed once per add_cpr_info() call, including multiple ages; modulus-11 no longer allocates a digit matrix. ISO reference dates are validated directly without parsing and formatting them through POSIXlt.

  • clean_cpr() returns already standardised character vectors without copying them. Cleaning remains optional before add_cpr_info() and is useful when standardising identifiers for joins or export.

  • Source installations now require a C compiler (Rtools on Windows).

  • Replace the experimental drop_all_na() with drop_empty_rows() and drop_empty_cols(). Both accept tidyselect column selections, including where(is.numeric), plus blank = TRUE for empty/whitespace-only text.

Developed by Daniel Madsen.
